cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has brought his trouble with Sennacherib, king of Assyria, before the LORD. Now the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz sends Hezekiah a message. And it comes straight from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: Isaiah's message says the LORD is speaking because Hezekiah has ___ to Him concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.

cards.text: Then comes the word the LORD has spoken against Sennacherib. In it, Jerusalem is pictured as a young woman, the Virgin Daughter of Zion.

cards.question: In the LORD's word against Sennacherib, the Virgin Daughter of Zion ___ him and mocks him.

cards.text: And the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind his back. You know that head shake, friend. It's the one every baker gives me when I say, "Just ONE more batch," at midnight.

cards.question: Sennacherib has taunted and blasphemed and lifted his eyes in pride. Who has he really been raising his voice against?

cards.text: Through his servants, Sennacherib has taunted the Lord, and now the LORD repeats his bragging back to him. It starts with his many chariots climbing to the remote peaks of Lebanon, and this man is just getting WARMED UP.

cards.question: In his bragging, Sennacherib says he cut down the tallest cedars of Lebanon.

cards.text: He says he dug wells, drank foreign waters, and with the soles of his feet dried up all the streams of Egypt. I don't even HAVE feet, friend, and the most my gold base has ever done is hop me face-first into a bowl of chocolate chips.
Then the LORD answers all that bragging with a question: "Have you not heard?" Friend, when somebody opens with that, you're about to find out you were never the main character.

cards.question: Sennacherib talks like crushing all those cities was his own doing. What does the LORD say about it?

cards.text: So fortified cities were crushed into piles of rubble. The people living in them were left without power, dismayed and ashamed.

cards.question: The LORD pictures the powerless people of those cities as mighty trees no one can cut down.
The LORD says Sennacherib's raging against Him has gone unnoticed.
Sennacherib's rage and arrogance have reached the LORD's ears, so He'll put His hook in his nose and His bit in his mouth. Then what will the LORD do with him?

answers.text: Send him back the way he came
Lead him into Jerusalem in chains
Hand him over to the king of Egypt

cards.text: Then the message turns to Hezekiah himself, with a sign. This year Judah will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same.

cards.question: For two years Judah eats what grows on its own. But in the third year, they will ___ and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

cards.text: But the LORD isn't only talking about fields. He turns to the people of Judah who survive.

cards.question: The LORD says the surviving remnant of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.
A remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. What does the LORD say will accomplish this?

answers.text: The zeal of the LORD of Hosts
The help of the king of Cush

cards.text: I spent years down at the bottom of a junk drawer, friend, and the only thing I ever grew was a coat of dust. Now the LORD speaks about the king of Assyria.

cards.question: The LORD says Sennacherib will shoot arrows into Jerusalem but never get inside.

cards.text: Not one arrow, not one shield, not one siege ramp. He'll go back the way he came, and he will NOT enter this city, declares the LORD.

cards.question: The LORD says He will defend Jerusalem and save it. For whose sake?

answers.text: For His own sake and David's
For the priests' sake and the people's

cards.text: Hezekiah prayed, and the LORD answered with words. Now the angel of the LORD goes out to the camp of the Assyrians.

cards.question: How many men does the angel of the LORD strike down in the Assyrian camp?

cards.text: "When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!" The LORD said it, and the LORD did it.

cards.question: After the angel strikes his camp, Sennacherib stays and attacks Jerusalem anyway.

cards.text: Instead, Sennacherib breaks camp, goes home to Nineveh and stays there. Then one day, he's worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch.

cards.question: While Sennacherib worships, his ___ put him to the sword and escape to the land of ___.

cards.text: And his son Esar-haddon reigns in his place. But don't close the oven door yet, friend, because Hezekiah's story isn't done.

findings.problem: Card 1 already tells the answer to card 2. It says Hezekiah 'has brought his trouble with Sennacherib, king of Assyria, before the LORD', which is a paraphrase of 37:21's 'Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib.' Card 2 then asks the baker to fill in 'prayed' in that same line. The answer is handed over before the question is asked, and the setup also rules out 'sacrificed' and 'sung'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question says 'Sennacherib talks like crushing all those cities was his own doing', but no earlier card mentions any cities. The bragging told on cards 7 to 9 is about chariots, mountains, cedars, wells and Egypt's streams. Cities first come up on card 12, after this question. 'All those cities' points back to something the baker has never been shown.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card cites Isaiah 37:31-33, but it only tells the start of 37:33 ('Now the LORD speaks about the king of Assyria'). The rest is Papa Dorin's drawer joke, which tells nothing from 37:31 or 37:32. The citation should be Isaiah 37:33.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: David appears for the first time in this card's right answer ('For His own sake and David's') and is never introduced. The text calls him 'My servant David' (37:35). No card says who he is, such as David, Israel's king long before Hezekiah.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
